latin: Anima in corpore, mens in anima, in mente uerbum, tum horum pater deus.
translator: original translation, drafted 2026-09-26 by WRITER-full-batch10, from Latin at farmer1998:17248
translation: Soul is in body, mind is in soul, in mind is the word, and God is the father of these three.
translation_note: Rendered directly from the Latin at farmer1998:17248, taking 'tum horum pater deus' as naming God the father of the three preceding terms, body, soul and mind, rather than of the word alone (farmer1998:17248).
doctrine: The thesis states a graded procession from body through soul and mind to the word, naming God as the father of the series (farmer1998:17248). The thesis is headed, in the edition consulted, 'Conclusio secundum priscam doctrinam Mercurii Trismegisti Aegyptii', which frames it as a report of Hermetic doctrine rather than Pico's own claim (kabbalah_paradigma:1397). Farmer pairs it with the following thesis, 27.4, and directs comparison to thesis 22.12 of Porphyry (farmer1998:17338).
historiography: A study of Pico's Kabbalistic epistemology cites this thesis by its full rubric and text at page 340 of the edition it consults, grouping it in a footnote with theses 22.12 and 3>49 and referring the reader to Cadafaz de Matos's study of Pico for further discussion, without stating in the passage consulted what connects the three theses (kabbalah_paradigma:1397).

quotations.text: Conclusio secundum priscam doctrinam Mercurii Trismegisti Aegyptii, 27.3.
Anima in corpore, mens in anima, in mente verbum, tum horum pater deus.

not_established: What specifically connects theses 22.12, 3>49 and 27.3 in the study's footnote is not established by the sources consulted; kabbalah_paradigma:1397 gives only the citation, not the argument.
The full text of thesis 22.12 of Porphyry, cross-referenced by Farmer's note, is not given in this packet and is not reproduced here.
